What Is Automotive Engineering? INTRODUCTION Automotive engineering applies engineering principles to the design, analysis, manufacture and operation of road vehicles. Motor vehicles are used to transport goods or passengers or to perform specific functions on land. The course focuses on non-guided ground vehicles and their major mechanical and vehicle systems. Automotive engineering integrates mechanics, materials, power transmission, fluids, controls and safety. Vehicle = integrated system Power Transmission Tires Vehicle motion

Vehicle Classification INTRODUCTION By guidance / running gear Guided vehicles: move along a fixed guide way, e.g., railway vehicles. Non-guided vehicles: can move in any direction; these are the main subject of the book. Single-track: two wheels, with or without a sidecar. Multi-track: three or more wheels. By application Passenger cars and buses. Pick-ups, vans and trucks. Tractors and special-purpose vehicles. Transport vehicles can also be classified by body type and load capacity.

Vehicle Types and Load Capacity INTRODUCTION Passenger car: intended for carrying up to nine passengers with luggage. Bus: designed to transport more than nine passengers and luggage. City buses emphasize rapid passenger turnover through low steps, wide doors and low floors. Tour buses are designed for long-distance comfort and provide substantial luggage space. Truck classes in the source range from extra-light-duty vehicles to extra-heavy-duty vehicles. Extra-light ≤0.75 t Light 0.75–2.5 t Medium 2.5–5 t Heavy 5–10 t Extra-heavy >10 t

ISO-Based Vehicle Classification & Drive Layouts INTRODUCTION ISO 3833 groups ground vehicles into categories such as motorbikes, traveler cars, buses, pickup trucks, agricultural machinery, trailer cars and semi-trailers. Drive arrangements described in the source include front- engine/front-wheel drive, front-engine/rear-wheel drive, rear- engine/rear-wheel drive and four-wheel drive. Engine/transmission placement strongly influences packaging and power flow.

Automatic gear box 13 An Automatic Transmission (AT) is a vehicle transmission system that automatically changes gear ratios according to vehicle speed, engine load, accelerator position, and driving conditions, without requiring the driver to operate a clutch pedal.
Main Components of an Automatic Transmission

Torque Converter 15 The torque converter is a hydro dynamic coupling located between the engine and the automatic gearbox. It allows the engine to continue running while the vehicle is stopped and transfers torque to the transmission through fluid motion. Main components Impeller (Pump): Connected to the engine and accelerates transmission fluid. Turbine: Connected to the transmission input shaft and receives torque from the moving fluid. Stator: Redirects returning fluid to improve torque transfer and provide torque multiplication. Lock-up clutch: Mechanically connects the engine and transmission input under suitable operating conditions to reduce slip.

Torque Converter 16 Step-by-step operation: The engine rotates the impeller. The impeller accelerates the transmission fluid. The moving fluid strikes the turbine blades, producing torque. The turbine rotates the transmission input shaft. The fluid returns through the stator, which redirects it during torque multiplication. At appropriate cruising conditions, the lock-up clutch can engage, reducing energy losses.

Planetary Gear Set 17 The planetary gear set is responsible for generating different gear ratios. Instead of sliding gears into and out of mesh, the transmission changes which planetary components are driven, held stationary, or connected to the output shaft.

Automatic gear box Operating steps: 1. The engine produces rotational power. 2. The clutch connects the engine to the gearbox. 3. When the driver presses the clutch pedal, the engine is disconnected from the transmission. 4. The driver moves the gear lever to select the required gear. 5. The synchronize r matches the rotational speeds of the components before engagement. 6. The driver releases the clutch, and power is transmitted to the wheels. Advantages: Simple construction, high efficiency, low manufacturing cost, and direct driver control. Disadvantages: Requires manual operation and can be tiring in heavy traffic.

Continuously Variable Transmission (CVT) 19 Working Principle A Continuously Variable Transmission changes the transmission ratio smoothly without using a fixed sequence of gear ratios. A common automotive CVT uses two adjustable pulleys connected by a steel belt or chain. Main components: Primary pulley (driving pulley) Secondary pulley (driven pulley) Steel belt or chain Hydraulic or electromechanical pulley control Transmission Control Unit (TCU)

Continuously Variable Transmission (CVT) 20 Operating steps The engine rotates the primary pulley. The belt transfers power to the secondary pulley. The effective diameters of both pulleys are adjusted. Changing the pulley diameters changes the transmission ratio. The control system continuously adjusts the ratio according to vehicle speed and engine load.

Continuously Variable Transmission (CVT) 22 Advantages: Smooth acceleration, continuously adjustable ratios, and the ability to maintain efficient engine operating speeds. Disadvantages: Belt or chain loading limitations, specialized maintenance requirements, and a driving feel that differs from fixed-gear transmissions.

Dual-Clutch Transmission (DCT) Operating steps 1. The vehicle moves in first gear through Clutch 1. 2. Second gear is pre selected on the other gear shaft. 3. When the control unit requests an up shift, Clutch 1 begins disengaging. 4. Simultaneously, Clutch 2 begins engaging. 5. Engine torque transfers from the first gear path to the second gear path. 6. Third gear can then be pre selected for the next shift. This overlapping clutch operation enables very fast gear changes with minimal interruption of wheel torque. Advantages: Rapid shifting, high mechanical efficiency, and good acceleration. Disadvantages: Complex mechanical and electronic control systems, potentially expensive repairs, and possible low-speed hesitation or clutch wear in some designs.
